_comment: EXAMPLE — Copilot enterprise managed settings. Not loaded from this path.
Deploy this file as `managed-settings.json` to the machine-wide location for
your platform via MDM/Intune/Jamf. It applies across VS Code, Copilot CLI,
the Copilot app, and the Copilot cloud agent. Developers cannot override it.
Settings combine ADDITIVELY with team-level overrides, so an org baseline and
a team supplement merge rather than replace one another.
Copy this into your own admin repo and delete what you do not enforce —
an over-broad managed policy is how teams end up disabling Copilot entirely.
_comment_plugins: Agent Plugins 1.0 packages skills + MCP servers into one installable unit.
That is convenient for developers and a supply-chain surface for you: a
plugin can ship an MCP server that reaches the network and a skill that
tells the agent to use it. Govern installs, not just usage.
enabledPlugins  — true force-installs, false blocks. Anything unlisted
stays at the developer's discretion unless

_comment_models: Restricting the roster is how you control spend and data residency.
Claude Fable 5 in particular requires explicit organisational enablement
because of Anthropic's data-retention behaviour for safety classification —
leave it out unless someone has actually signed off on that.
Re-check this list against .github/model-compatibility.json each quarter:
o3, o4-mini, gpt-4.1, gemini-2.5-pro and gemini-2.0-flash are already gone,
and Claude Sonnet 4.5/4.6 and Opus 4.5/4.6 retire 2026-09-01.
_comment_hooks: Administrator-deployed hooks are machine-wide, cannot be disabled by the
developer, and are CLI-only. Use them for audit logging and hard gates.
Remember the failure modes: timeouts always fail OPEN, and preToolUse
command hooks fail CLOSED on non-timeout errors. A policy hook that is
slow degrades to no policy at all, so keep it fast and keep the timeout
generous enough that a cold start does not silently disable the gate.
